$comment: Antigravity CLI on a Google AI Pro/Ultra subscription.
STOP. Read `cache.kind` before using anything in this file.
Google prices context caching as STORAGE OVER TIME - a per-token-hour charge for keeping a
cache alive - not as a write multiplier against a TTL the way Anthropic does. The two are not
the same arithmetic wearing different numbers, and no conversion between them was found that
could be defended. Under a subscription the user-visible currency is neither: it is quota, and
no public figure maps Antigravity's quota onto cached tokens.
So `cache.kind` is `unpriced`, which is a real state the code understands: CostModel.canPriceCache()
returns false, and the cache clock refuses to spend on keepalive or compaction for this provider
rather than acting on an invented number. A worker on this model still runs work, still gets
preempted at a window boundary, and still hands off - it simply will not pay to hold a cache
open, because nobody here knows what that costs.
This file becomes useful the moment somebody measures it. Until then its honesty is its value:
an invented multiplier would be indistinguishable from a measured one at the point of use.
MODELS: read from `agy models` on 2026-08-25 (agy 1.1.20), not guessed. Note two things.
First, effort is baked into the model id (-high/-medium/-low) as well as being a --effort flag.
Second, Antigravity serves Claude and GPT-OSS models alongside Gemini - so 'this task needs
Claude' does NOT imply 'this task needs a claude-code worker', and capability routing has to be
asked about the model, not the vendor.

cache.$comment: Google bills cache STORAGE per token-hour. Not a TTL multiplier, and not converted here.

quota.$comment: Two separately metered pools on one account - Gemini apart from Claude/GPT - measured 2026-08-27 by reading the `/usage` panel, which renders both groups' windows. This block previously said kind 'unknown', probe 'none', windows [], which contradicted both the adapter's quotaProbe: 'cli' and a parser that had been reading four windows for two days. The ids here are what parseUsageScreen emits; the exact group slug follows the panel's heading wording, so `pool` is matched by containment rather than by equality.

$owed: Cache pricing: is it storage-per-token-hour on a subscription at all, or is caching simply not billed to a subscriber? Until this is known, cache.kind stays `unpriced`.
Context windows are the published figures for each family, not read from the CLI - `agy models` reports ids and display names only.
Whether a quota window exists at all, and over what period. /usage and /credits are slash commands; HANDOFF R9 measures whether print mode runs them for free.
Nothing here is metered: agy writes conversations as SQLite, so the transcript tailer reads nothing. See capabilities.meteredFromTranscript.
